title: Mountain Echo ABC
hook: Rock gives back a sound, then the valley lets it go.
roundStructure: Round 1 lexical-semantic A-Z; Round 2 retrieval-action A-Z; 4+4+4+4+4+4+2 chunks
responseSpace: one beat of quiet before answer
visualStyle: sunny 3D mountain storybook, alpine green and sky blue, friendly wildlife, clear layered peaks and isolated subjects

creativeFingerprint.pointOfView: a child making one careful call from a safe viewpoint and listening to how distance changes sound
creativeFingerprint.chorusFunction: turn call-return-fade into a memory reset without echoing over the target word
creativeFingerprint.grooveMeter: measured 4/4 with one-beat echo pockets and long valley tails
creativeFingerprint.round1Grammar: hand-written distance-and-sound scenes; silent targets are visual anchors and unsafe cliff/ledge/summit cues remain viewpoint-only
creativeFingerprint.round2Grammar: call or sight cue -> recall gap -> target -> safe point/listen gesture
creativeFingerprint.sectionContrast: Verses stay sparse; chorus widens; retrieval strips back. small echo responses after targets, with acoustic walking pulse
creativeFingerprint.signatureColor: small echo responses after targets, with acoustic walking pulse
creativeFingerprint.authorialIntent: Use real mountain echo as the memory device: hard rock returns sound, open valleys soften it, and each target either belongs to the landscape or is framed honestly as a helper object.
creativeFingerprint.lyricIdentity: A child calls once and listens to what comes back; the song alternates close rock, far ridge, bird flight, water and fading echo rather than shouting every line twice.
semanticArc: living and nonliving mountain clues answer differently
water and altitude widen the sound field
echo fades into the final switchback
forbiddenGenericLanguage: highland words come back to me
